answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may vote on a market or claim a reward. The protocol caps influence by stake and destroys part of it when an identity is proven to double-vote, so splitting one budget across a thousand names does not create a thousand independent voices. A real newcomer can enter through an inlet, perhaps after reading a sonnet, but the sybil attacker must tie up capital for every identity and risks losing it; the ledge is the cost of capital, not a claim that staking makes identities impossible to fake.
